# The voucher census sent as an AlterID span: BRIDGE TRANSFER LAB and BRIDGE OUTSTANDINGS LAB (#899, part 2)

These files are the six requests and eight answers of a read-only lab run of 26 October 2026 on two synthetic books, one at a time, each the only company loaded (TallyPrime 7.2, Silver, licensed mode, Education mode off): BRIDGE TRANSFER LAB (18:33 UTC) and BRIDGE OUTSTANDINGS LAB (18:34 UTC for its first attempt, 18:53 UTC for the run kept here). On each book the run read the company marks, the voucher census of a window as master sends it (no AlterID filter), the same census spanned to the voucher mark (`$AlterID > 0 AND $AlterID <= M`), and the marks again. Each request is the code's own rendering and differs from its unspanned partner only by that filter. They were sent one at a time with `curl.exe --data-binary`, each answer written straight to a file and never piped; every send returned HTTP 200 with curl exit 0. The status check before each book came from the 0.6.0 build of `bridge_mcp` over stdio with posting and import off; it showed that one company, release 7.2, licence tier silver.

The answers were published on the branch `lab/899-spanned-census-answers` (commit `6c8ff7c7`) with a hash table: book T under `answers/`, book O under `answers/book-o-from-eeb25c83/`. The requests are on `lab/899-spanned-census-captures` (commit `eeb25c83`), checked against that branch's hash list before the first send of each book (8 of 8). Each file here is byte-equal to the file there and its SHA-256 equals the one in that table. The evidence folders were zipped on the lab PC (sha256 `76f19820afe559d4295cca01963c30280d38f8647fa981360673db2777ea276d` for the first run, `8cd8873af53d40f1bfec45de9bcb28bb069979f9a87aa7062794b26ab2b6dbf4` for book O's second); the files are unedited.

The data is synthetic: BRIDGE TRANSFER LAB holds five Contras between two bank ledgers keyed by hand on 3 to 5 April 2026; BRIDGE OUTSTANDINGS LAB holds 17 vouchers in the window read. No GSTIN, PAN or contact detail appears in either answer.

## What the answers show

- Book T: marks `ALTVCHID` 5 and `ALTMSTID` 210 before and after; the census and the census spanned to (0, 5] are byte-equal; 5 vouchers, counted by structure (nodes named exactly `VOUCHER` under `ENVELOPE/BODY/DATA/COLLECTION`, parsed as XML, not by substring).
- Book O: marks `ALTVCHID` 21 and `ALTMSTID` 222 before and after; the census and the census spanned to (0, 21] are byte-equal; 17 vouchers, counted the same way.
- The same two books gave byte-equal censuses with and without the span at marks 5 and 21. In both, every voucher's alteration id is at most the mark.

## Book O's mark: 20 to 21 is UNVERIFIED

The first run sheet rendered book O's spanned request for the voucher mark 20, the mark the book had last shown. The first attempt on 26 October read the marks first and found 21, so its stop rule fired and only that marks read was kept (`answers/o-m1.response`). The request was rendered again for 21 and the book read again; the second run is the one kept here. That the mark is 21 is established: three reads of it (the first attempt's, and the second run's before and after) are byte-equal. Why it is 21 and not 20, what moved it and when, is not established: no voucher in the window carries alteration id 21 (the highest is 20), and alteration ids 1, 4 and 9 are not in the window either, so the move cannot be traced to a voucher this window holds. The byte-equality at mark 21 stands on its own; nothing here shows that a book whose mark has moved since the span was rendered answers the same.

## What they do not show

Two books, one release (7.2), one run each. No voucher in either window has an alteration id above the mark, so a span that leaves a voucher out was not exercised. A larger book, or a census a span would truncate, was not read.
